method: Independent inspection of the actual baseline and candidate face crops and full stage PNGs from the three completed native browser runs, with SHA256 hashes of all twelve files.
observations: In the infant contrast face crop and narrow stage view, the candidate gives the lower nose edge a thin, readable curved outline. It stays separate from the mouth and supporting hand and does not form a dark filled patch.

In the recovered adult contrast face crop and stage view, the candidate makes the nose contour visible where the baseline white feature largely blends into the face. The restrained line follows the nose edge without an obvious protrusion or heavy shadow.

The normal adult baseline and candidate PNGs have identical file hashes for both face and stage. The inspected normal view retains the same nose, lip finish, skin shading, hand placement and head silhouette.

Across the contrast comparisons, the head silhouette, supporting hand, eyelid marks and mouth appearance are visually unchanged. The added nose contour remains localized and does not compete with the hand placement demonstration.
limitations: This review covers twelve static PNGs from three selected native browser views, including one normal-mode control and two contrast-mode views. It does not assess every age, pose, camera angle or motion frame.
The images come from the raw-module browser harness. This visual review does not validate the full application loader, build or deployment.
The earlier adult contrast attempt is excluded because its wrapper exceeded the total deadline; acceptance uses the completed recovered run.
